projection.rationale: Revenue rises QoQ on seasonal demand uptick and initial Korba Phase-II Unit 1 commissioning late in the quarter. OPM improves from Q4FY26's 33.3% to 37.5% driven by better PLF and higher capacity charges from new PPAs, though partial Korba ramp limits full benefit. PAT boosted by lower tax charge trend seen in Q4FY26.

Sequential revenue growth from full quarter contribution of Korba Unit 1 and start of Unit 2. OPM expands to ~38.6% as new capacity charges kick in. PAT growth aided by operational leverage and sustained lower tax rate.
Revenue peaks on full Korba Phase-II operations and seasonal demand. OPM stable near 39% as fuel pass-through protects margins. PAT growth YoY strong due to absence of one-offs and lower tax charge.

Full-year Korba contribution and improved PLF drive revenue and EBITDA to FY27 highs. OPM near 40% reflecting stable capacity charges and cost pass-through. PAT growth YoY aided by lower tax and higher EBITDA.

bull_bear.body:
- Conservative; majority of expansion funded by internal accruals over time, interim bridge via NCDs/corporate debt.
- ~INR20,000 cr annualized FFO; FY26 operational cash flow ~INR21,000 cr.
- Could repay entire debt by FY31–32 → potential debt-free; large surplus thereafter to be redeployed (thermal now, nuclear/hydro/overseas later). No dividend/buyback discussed.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- Merchant-price compression as RE capacity scales (mgmt's explicit thesis for de-risking via PPAs).
- Execution/commissioning slippage from geopolitical labour & LPG/critical-resource availability (already pushed Mahan).
- Bangladesh (BPDB) receivables: outstanding down, regular payments resuming; disputed amount with appointed expert, could escalate to Singapore arbitration (SIAC).
- Rising leverage (net debt INR45,022 cr) during build phase.
- Demand sensitivity to weather (early/extended monsoon depressed FY26 demand to +0.8%).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and execution-focused; transparent on the downward near-term capacity revision (framing as deferral, not cut) and on Mahan delay drivers. Repeatedly anchors to FY31–32 targets and conservative funding posture. Candid that PPA-vs-merchant realization is not forecastable.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The 27% reported EBITDA jump is partly acquisition-driven (Moxie/Vidarbha); continuing EBITDA only +9% — watch the "reported vs continuing" gap.
- Merchant capacity collapse to 5% caps upside in high-price quarters but materially de-risks the RE-driven price decline mgmt expects.
- MSEDCL 2.5 GW RE-RTC routes most economics to AGEL (renewables + batteries), not APL — APL contribution is marginal residual coal.
- Nuclear/Bhutan-hydro are early optionality, not near-term earnings; nuclear gated entirely on pending GoI SMR rules.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Deleveraging is the headline capital story: net debt / continuing EBITDA fell from 9.75x in FY19 to 2.12x at Jun'26 (TTM), and senior term debt / equity from 5.32x in Mar'20 to 0.66x at Jun'26.
- Growth is described as largely self-funded — the majority of capital expenditure is to be funded through internal accruals, supported by an effectively unlevered capital structure and significant free cash flow to equity.
- Credit profile upgraded 8 notches over six years with coverage widening from one to four rating agencies, most now at AA/Stable, on the back of high PPA tie-ups and stable operations.
- Balance sheet at Jun'26: gross debt Rs 58,381 Cr, cash Rs 10,739 Cr, net debt Rs 47,643 Cr (Rs 2.60 Cr/MW), net fixed assets Rs 1,09,698 Cr at 2.30x net debt.
- Returns profile on a TTM Jun'26 basis: RoA 15.3%, RoCE 19.5%, RoE 22.6%; the deck makes no mention of dividends or buybacks.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Moxie Power** (ex-Coastal Energen, full-year consolidation in FY26): drove minority-interest jump (Q3 INR8.5 cr → Q4 INR254 cr) after 558 MW medium-term PPA with Tamil Nadu for Unit 2.
- **Vidarbha**: 600 MW operating capacity acquired during FY26, added to fixed assets (explains 25% net-fixed-asset jump vs ~6–7% capacity growth, rest is CWIP).
- **MSEDCL 2.5 GW RE-RTC**: group product — thermal (APL) + renewable & batteries (AGEL) + PSP, served via a to-be-created group trading platform; only residual ~1–1.5% APL coal capacity feeds in.
- **JAL/JPVL resolution**: APL as implementing agency takes 180 MW asset + JAL's 24% stake in JPVL; JPVL stations Nigrie, Bina, Vishnuprayag.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary stock(s) | Loser | Why / conviction |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rising baseload demand + states chasing resource adequacy (13.8 GW+ PPA bids) | ADANIPOWER · 533096; NTPC (code unverified) | — | PPA-backed thermal IPPs with shovel-ready capacity win firm long-term offtake. High |
| RE penetration suppressing merchant tariffs | ADANIPOWER · 533096 (95% tied up) | Merchant-heavy thermal/IPPs (code unverified) | Players still exposed to spot prices face margin erosion; APL de-risked. High |

| Imported-coal price/shipping pressure | ADANIPOWER · 533096 | — | Fuel fully pass-through under PPAs; insulated. High |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- India's largest private-sector thermal IPP with an 18,330 MW operating portfolio of 13 assets across 9 states, plus a 40 MWp solar plant at Bitta; part of the Adani infrastructure and utility portfolio.
- Positioned as the base-load complement to renewables: the deck argues India needs 97 GW of additional coal-based capacity by FY35, with base-load capacity rising from 247 GW (Dec'25) to 309 GW by FY32E alongside 500 GW renewables by 2030.
- Dominant share of the recent thermal PPA cycle: of 20.9 GW of SHAKTI-linked PPAs awarded by state discoms, APL won 13.9 GW (roughly two-thirds), and 12.6 GW of the 19.3 GW awarded in the last two financial years.
- Track record framed around acquisition and turnaround of 7.5 GW of stressed assets, giving 41% inorganic share of the operating portfolio and economies of scale.
- Rated India's Most Valued Energy Brand 2026 by Brand Finance, with brand value of USD 1.8 billion and AAA rating.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] Acquired the power assets of Jaiprakash Associates Ltd. in Q1 FY27 for Rs 4,194 Crore, including a 180 MW Churk plant (Uttar Pradesh) to be revived.
- [Financial stakes] The Jaiprakash transaction also brings a 24% equity stake in 2,220 MW Jaiprakash Power Ventures Ltd. and an 11% stake in 1,980 MW Prayagraj Power Generation Company Ltd.
- [Policy] SHAKTI policy clause B(iv) coal allocations of ~30 GW to state discoms are driving a fresh wave of long-term thermal PPA bids, the direct source of APL's locked-in growth.
- [Governance] Board is 40% independent directors, with 100% of statutory committees chaired by independent directors, plus six additional business-specific committees, independent third-party review of related-party transactions, and ID tenure capped at two three-year terms.
- [New subsidiary] Adani Atomic Energy Ltd. incorporated as a wholly owned subsidiary to enter nuclear power generation.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- Fuel cost is pass-through under PPAs; states secure fuel allocation for winning bidders (de-risks fuel availability).
- Imported-coal PPA tariffs lower YoY on lower import coal prices (revenue optically softer but pass-through protects margin).
- New PPAs carry "materially better capacity charges" → improving return metrics; availability-based fixed charges give stable per-MW EBITDA.
- No domestic coal shortage; only shipping/bunker cost uptick on imports (passed through).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- Merchant capacity 16% (start FY26) → ~5% now; further declines as Vidarbha/Karnataka/Coastal tie-ups land.
- New 1,600 MW MSEDCL LoA secured this quarter (total expansion tie-up 11.7 → 13.3 GW).
- Minority interest jumped Q3 INR8.5 cr → Q4 INR254 cr on TN 558 MW medium-term PPA for Moxie Unit 2 + full-year Coastal consolidation.
- FY27/FY28 capacity-add guidance revised DOWN vs last quarter (FY27 2.9→1.32 GW; FY28 2.4→1.6 GW); Mahan slipped from Dec target toward Q1 FY28.
- INR7,500 cr secured NCDs raised; net debt up on capex bridge financing.
- Bhutan 570 MW hydro SPV and multiple nuclear SPVs newly incorporated.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log

outlook.body:
- **FY27 capacity add: 1.32 GW (Korba Phase-II)** — Unit 1 commissioning Q2 FY27 (Jun–Sep), Unit 2 before year-end. **VERIFY next quarter.**
- FY28 add: ~1.6 GW (Mahan Phase-II) — first unit targeted end-FY27, slips to Q1 FY28 if geopolitical labour/LPG constraints persist.
- Korba FY27 EBITDA contribution ~INR1,000 cr (partial year), higher in FY28 (full year + PPA).
- Capex: FY27 ~INR25,000 cr; FY28 ~INR33,000 cr. Total expansion program ~INR2 lakh cr.
- FY27 PLF expected "far better" than Q1 FY26; demand recovery visible from Mar.
- INR50,000 cr EBITDA target by FY31 (possibly FY30).
- Cost of borrowing ~8% (DCM/domestic banks).
outlook.title: Guidance (verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
- 95% of 18.15 GW operating capacity tied under long/medium-term PPA; merchant down to **5%** (from 16% at start of FY26).
- 13.3 GW long-term PPAs tied for the 23.7 GW expansion (10.4 GW tied during FY26).
- New: 1,600 MW LoA from Maharashtra DISCOM (MSEDCL); PPA not yet signed, expects sign in ~3 months then 48-month build → commissioning in 4–5 yrs; likely allocated to Raigarh / Raipur / Korba. Tariff INR5.30/unit (INR4.11 capacity + INR1.19 energy).
- Market pipeline: ~13.8 GW PPA bids out (UP, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand, West Bengal, Gujarat); Gujarat issued additional 4,000 MW bid doc.
- Rajasthan 3.2 GW tie-up still pending.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **Hydro**: 570 MW Bhutan hydro SPV incorporated; evaluating thermal/hydro/transmission beyond India.
- **Nuclear**: several Indian SPVs incorporated; awaiting GoI rules (SMR clarity); identifying NEW (non-thermal) sites. National target 9 GW → 100 GW framed as large opportunity.
- Group trading platform for bundled RTC products.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: A merchant-light, PPA-heavy thermal IPP compounding EBITDA through a funded 23.7 GW thermal build-out to FY32, with optionality in hydro/nuclear and a credible path to ~INR50,000 cr EBITDA and potential debt-free status by FY31–32.

Two units targeted next year to achieve 40% technical minimum under the government's flexible operation trajectory.
Korba Phase-II first unit to commission Jun-Sep 2026 (Q2), second unit before FY27 year-end.

Reviving and completing the 1,320 MW Korba (ex-Lanco Amarkantak) expansion, commissioning of balance work in about 30 months.
Expansion capex of ~INR 25,000 crores in FY27 (adding 1.32 GW Korba) and ~INR 33,000 crores in FY28 (adding 1.6 GW Mahan).
Total capex for Mahan Phase-II is INR 13,500 crores with major packages including BTG already ordered from BHEL.
Mahan Energen Phase-II 1600 MW ultra-supercritical expansion at Singrauli to be commissioned by FY27-28.
Targeting addition of 12,520 MW by 2030; achieved rapid progress on 4,800 MW of this.
Expanding capacity to 30,670 MW by 2030 via three 1600 MW brownfield projects (Mahan, Raipur, Raigarh) plus Korba revival.
Targeting more than 30 GW of operating capacity by 2030.
Advance orders given to main plant supplier (BHEL) for 11.2 GW of capacity to be commissioned phase-wise by FY30.
Targeting 30+ GW of operating capacity by FY30, out of targeted organic addition of 12.5 GW.
Targeting total capacity of 30.67 GW by FY29-30 via brownfield expansion and inorganic opportunities.
Expects to reach INR 50,000 crore EBITDA conservatively by FY2031 (possibly FY2030 if no issues arise).
By FY31-32 able to repay entire debt with large cash surplus thereafter; potential debt-free company with new deployment (incl. nuclear) opportunities.
Adding 23.7 GW of thermal capacity by 2032 to reach 42 GW total; on track for ~34 GW by FY30.
By FY31-32 cash flow sufficient to repay entire debt and still have significant surplus, potentially becoming debt-free.
Progressing on a 23.7 GW thermal expansion program to reach 42 GW total capacity by FY31-32.
